title: Constructible preservation before biduality
statement: Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\geq1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with structure morphism $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Work in the ordinary derived category $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ for its bounded constructible complexes [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] having Tor amplitude in some finite interval [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Let $a_X^{\times}$ be the ambient right adjoint to ordinary etale compact-support direct image $Ra_{X!}$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], put $\omega_X=a_X^{\times}A$, and write $D_X=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,\omega_X)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then $D_X$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ into itself. More precisely, for $d\in\mathbf N$, integers $a,b$, and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ with $\dim X\leq d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, the complex $D_XK$ has Tor amplitude in $[-b-2d,-a]$. This bound is independent of $n$.

proof.text: If $a>b$, testing the Tor condition with $M=A_X$ and using [lem-kun-tensor-unit] makes every cohomology sheaf of $K$ zero, so $K=0$ and $D_XK=0$; the assertion holds even for the empty interval. Assume henceforth $a\leq b$. Choose, by [lem-sf-etale-smooth-stratified-ctf], a finite partition of the underlying space of $X$ by reduced, connected, smooth locally closed immersions $s_r:S_r\hookrightarrow X$, with pure dimensions $e_r\leq\dim X\leq d$. Put $P_r=s_r^{-1}K$. The cited statement supplies an etale covering of each $S_r$ on which $P_r$ is represented by a bounded complex $E_r^\bullet$ of constant finite projective $A$-modules, zero outside $[a,b]$. It also supplies finite locally constant cohomology of $P_r$. The theorem applies because $k$ is algebraically closed, $A$ is finite, and $K$ is bounded constructible with the stated Tor interval. If $X$ is empty its partition has no strata.

The same stratification theorem supplies objects $F_0=K,F_1,\ldots,F_m=0$ and distinguished triangles $G_r\to F_{r-1}\to F_r\to G_r[1]$, where $G_r=Rs_{r!}P_r$. Its statement also identifies $Rs_{r!}=j_!i_*$ for a closed-then-open factorization $s_r=ji$. We will prove the bound and bounded constructibility for $D_XG_r$, then recover $D_XF_{r-1}$ from $D_XF_r$ by the reverse induction written in step 5. No pro-etale recollement assertion is needed.

The field spectrum is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), so $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. In a factorization $S_r\xrightarrow{i}V\xrightarrow{j}X$, the open $V$ and each of its intersections with affine opens of $X$ are Noetherian and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Hence $j$ is quasi-compact and of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]. The closed immersion $i$ is of finite type: on affine opens its ring map is a quotient, generated as an algebra by the empty set [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Thus $S_r$ and $s_r$ are finite type, and $S_r$ is Noetherian by the same finite-type theorem. An immersion is separated since it is a monomorphism, whose diagonal is an isomorphism. Consequently all structure morphisms and stratum immersions here are separated of finite type between Noetherian schemes; [thm-nagata-compactification] supplies compactifications. Use the unbounded ordinary-etale composition isomorphism of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], including the closed/open factorizations, to identify $Ra_{X!}Rs_{r!}\cong Ra_{S_r!}$. The ambient adjoints exist by [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]; $s_r^!$ is the closed/open right adjoint specified in [lem-weil-stratum-ambient-hom]. For every $Q\in D(S_r{}_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $B\in D(\operatorname{Spec}k_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, the composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] gives the natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Q,s_r^!a_X^{\times}B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rs_{r!}Q,a_X^{\times}B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_{X!}Rs_{r!}Q,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_{S_r!}Q,B).$$
Thus $s_r^!a_X^{\times}$ and $a_{S_r}^{\times}$ are right adjoints of the same functor and identify by [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint]. In particular $s_r^!\omega_X\cong\omega_{S_r}$. The ambient identity [lem-weil-stratum-ambient-hom], with $M=\omega_X$, now gives
$$D_XG_r\cong Rs_{r*}R\mathcal Hom_A(P_r,s_r^!\omega_X)\cong Rs_{r*}D_{S_r}P_r.$$
Every adjunction and internal Hom in this calculation is ambient.

Apply [thm-asd-smooth-tensor] to the smooth compactifiable structure morphism $a_{S_r}$ of pure relative dimension $e_r$. Its base is Noetherian and the exponent of $A$ is invertible there. It gives $\omega_{S_r}=L_r[2e_r]$ with $L_r$ etale locally free of rank one. The restriction isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] lets us calculate $D_{S_r}P_r$ on a common covering trivializing $L_r$ and providing $E_r^\bullet$ from step 1. By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], this restriction is represented by
$$Q_r^\bullet=\mathcal Hom_A^\bullet(E_r^\bullet,A[2e_r]).$$
Indeed, $\mathcal Hom_A(E_r^i,-)$ is a direct summand of a finite power of the identity, hence is exact; the finite filtration by the source degrees therefore shows that $\mathcal Hom_A^\bullet(E_r^\bullet,-)$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Applying it to a K-injective resolution of $A[2e_r]$ justifies the displayed model. The Hom-complex degree formula gives $Q_r^j=\mathcal Hom_A(E_r^{-j-2e_r},A)$, so it is zero unless $-b-2e_r\leq j\leq-a-2e_r$, and each term is finite projective. Its cohomology is finite locally constant by the kernel/cokernel clauses of [lemma-constructible-flc-serre]. The flat-complex bound [lem-kun-flat-bounded-tor-amplitude] gives this Tor interval on every covering member. Derived tensor commutes with restriction by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], so the vanishing holds for every degree-zero module sheaf globally: its cohomology restricts to zero on a cover and is therefore zero. Thus $D_{S_r}P_r$ is bounded constructible with this interval.
The immersion $s_r$ is separated of finite type and its source has dimension $e_r$. Apply the all-module-sheaf vanishing assertion of [lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing] with $N=2e_r$ and then [thm-sf-direct-image-tor-amplitude]. They give bounded constructibility of $Rs_{r*}D_{S_r}P_r$ and the Tor interval $[-b-2e_r,-a]$, which is contained in $I=[-b-2d,-a]$.

By [lem-sf-hom-triangulated], applying $D_X$ to the triangles of step 2 gives distinguished triangles
$$D_XF_r\longrightarrow D_XF_{r-1}\longrightarrow D_XG_r\longrightarrow D_XF_r[1].$$
Start with $D_XF_m=D_X0=0$ and induct downwards on $r$. Suppose $D_XF_r$ is bounded constructible with Tor interval $I$; step 4 proves this for $D_XG_r$. For any degree-zero module sheaf $M$, [lem-kun-derived-tensor-triangulated] gives the tensor triangle, and the long exact sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] contains
$$\mathcal H^j(D_XF_r\otimes_A^LM)\longrightarrow\mathcal H^j(D_XF_{r-1}\otimes_A^LM)\longrightarrow\mathcal H^j(D_XG_r\otimes_A^LM).$$
Both outer terms vanish for $j\notin I$, so the middle term vanishes there. With $M=A_X$ this also bounds ordinary cohomology. For each $j$, the untensored long exact sequence writes $\mathcal H^j(D_XF_{r-1})$ as an extension of a cokernel of a map between constructible sheaves by a kernel of a map between constructible sheaves. These are constructible by [thm-constructible-serre]. This proves the induction claim, hence the assertion for $F_0=K$. For qualitative preservation, choose any Tor interval $[a,b]$ for $K$ and set $d_0=\max(\{0\}\cup\{e_r:1\leq r\leq m\})$; the same argument uses only $e_r\leq d_0$ and gives a finite interval without needing a previously chosen dimension bound. The quantitative common interval uses only $a,b,d$, not $n$. Finally $A_X$ has Tor interval $[0,0]$, and $R\mathcal Hom_A(A_X,\omega_X)\cong\omega_X$: in the K-injective model of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], the termwise identification $\mathcal Hom_A(A_X,J^i)=J^i$ commutes with the differentials. Thus $\omega_X$ is bounded constructible with Tor interval $[-2d,0]$.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X$ be separated of finite type over $k$.
Its ambient dualizing object is $\omega_X=Ra_X^{\times}A$.
Write $D_X=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,\omega_X)$.
Then $D_X$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$ into itself.
More precisely, if $\dim X\leq d$ and $K$ has Tor amplitude
in $[a,b]$, then $D_XK$ has Tor amplitude in
$[-b-2d,-a]$. This bound is independent of the exponent $n$.

proof.text:
Choose a finite stratification of $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ by smooth
locally closed subschemes $s:S\hookrightarrow X$ on which the
cohomology of $K$ is finite locally constant. Such a stratification
exists by constructibility, Noetherian induction, and the fact that a
reduced scheme over the perfect field $k$ has a dense smooth open in
each irreducible component. Nilpotent thickenings leave the etale site
unchanged. The finite-Tor restriction $P=s^*K$ is site-perfect:
successive local finite-free presentations give a bounded-above free
resolution, and truncation below the Tor bound leaves a finitely
presented flat last syzygy. This is the sheaf-local argument of
[lem-weil-bounded-finite-tor-perfect], with the notion of
[def-weil-site-perfect-complex]; it does not claim that each
cohomology module separately has finite projective dimension.

The open–closed triangles of
[def-weil-open-closed-recollement] build $K$, by finitely many
cones, from the objects $Rs_!P$. Ambient tensor adjunction gives

$$
D_XRs_!P\cong
Rs_*R\mathcal Hom_A(P,Rs^{\times}\omega_X)
=Rs_*D_SP.
$$

This is [lem-weil-stratum-ambient-hom] for the locally closed
immersion, using composition of right adjoints. It is an ambient
identity, so it assumes no constructible preservation by $D_X$.
On a stratum of dimension $r$, the ambient smooth theorem
[thm-asd-smooth-tensor] makes $\omega_S$ an invertible sheaf
shifted by $[2r]$. Thus $D_SP=P^\vee\otimes\omega_S$ is
a site-perfect complex of Tor amplitude
$[-b-2r,-a-2r]$. The direct-image
theorem [thm-sf-direct-image-tor-amplitude], with the uniform
vanishing bound of [lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing], makes
$Rs_*D_SP$ bounded constructible of Tor amplitude
$[-b-2r,-a]$, contained in $[-b-2d,-a]$.
The localization triangles assemble these pieces by extensions;
tensoring such a triangle with any module sheaf preserves the common
vanishing interval. Exactness of internal Hom in its first variable
therefore gives the stated bound for $D_XK$. Taking $K=A_X$ also proves that
$\omega_X$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude.
